newsitem.title: INDONESIA: TELKOM SAYS 1.6 MLN LINES UNSOLD - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: TELKOM SAYS 1.6 MLN LINES UNSOLD - REPORT.

text.p: Indonesia's state-controlled telecommunications firm PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia said some 1.6 million, or 30 percent, of its 5.6 million installed fixed telephone line capacity has not been sold yet, Kompas newspaper reported on Tuesday.

"Indonesia is so large. If it is grouped, there (will) always be lines which have not been sold yet. But the lines are not meant to be idle, they are just unsold," Telkom's president director Asman Akhir Nasution was quoted as saying by Kompas.
Telkom, also listed in New York, was trying to improve marketing and services to address the problem, Kompas quoted Nasution as saying.
The newspaper did not give further details. Telkom officials were not immediately available for comment.
